**`kwaipilot/kat-coder-v2.5-dev`** is an open-weight, Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) coding foundation model released by **Kwaipilot** (Kuaishou's AI team) optimized specifically for agentic software engineering and tool-use workflows.[1][2][3]

***

## Key Overview and Architecture

- **Base Architecture**: Mixture-of-Experts built on top of `Qwen3.6-35B-A3B`.[2]
- **Parameter Count**: 35 billion total parameters with **3B** actively routed per token.[1][2]
- **Modality**: Text-only; the open weights exclude multimodal and visual encoders.[2][1]
- **Context Length**: Up to 262,144 tokens (256K context window).[4][2]
- **License**: Apache 2.0 (open-weight, permissive for commercial applications).[2]

***

## Strengths and Training Highlights

- **Agentic Repository Coding**: Post-trained with large-scale supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning (RL) in executable repository environments to handle issue localization, multi-file code modifications, and autonomous bug fixing.[3][4][2]
- **High Benchmark Performance**: Achieves state-of-the-art results for its parameter class on benchmarks like SWE-bench Verified (~69.40%).[3]
- **Mitigated Pathological Behaviors**: RL training reduced single-turn repetition and drastically reduced tool label syntax errors (from 9.34% to 0.28%).[5]
- **Flexible Reasoning**: Supports dual modes, providing extended chain-of-thought reasoning traces as well as direct output modes.[3]

***

## Deployment and Ecosystem Support

- **Inference Engines**: Supported out-of-the-box by Hugging Face Transformers, vLLM, SGLang, and KTransformers.[1][2]
- **Local Quantization**: Quantized GGUF formats (via `bartowski`) allow local execution using `llama.cpp`, Ollama, LM Studio, and Jan AI.[6][7]
- **Agent Frameworks**: Compatible with developer agent toolchains such as Claude Code, OpenHands, and Kilo Code.[8][9][4]
